activities.anchor: Jan Baptista van Helmont grew a willow
activities.caption: rebuild the evidence chain — willow to equation
activities.name: phHistoryOrder

config.prompt: How humanity worked out the loop — put the experiments in order:
items: 1640s: van Helmont grows a willow in 91 kg of dried soil for five years, watering it only
The tree gains 74 kg while the soil loses almost nothing — mass does not come from soil
1771: Priestley seals a mouse and a lit candle in a jar; a sprig of mint 'restores the air'
Within a decade, Ingenhousz shows the restoration needs light
The pieces assemble into an equation: light + water + carbon dioxide → sugar + oxygen
config.why: Simple experiments, one hint at a time — the first hint that a plant's mass does not come from the soil, though van Helmont guessed water and CO₂ was still unknown.

activities.anchor: commercial greenhouse growers pump in extra
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the greenhouse's CO₂ top-up
activities.name: phGreenhouseEstimate

config.prompt: Outdoor air is about 0.04% carbon dioxide. Commercial greenhouse growers pump in extra to push photosynthesis past its light-limited plateau — about what concentration do they run?
config.why: About 0.1% — two-and-a-half times outdoors — because when light is no longer the limit, carbon dioxide or temperature takes over as the bottleneck.
config.context: The aquatic-plant classic: count oxygen bubbles per minute as the lamp moves closer — the count doubles, then stops responding.

activities.anchor: near-mirror images — but with completely different machinery
activities.caption: uphill build vs downhill burn — drag across the loop
activities.name: phMirrorCompare

config.prompt: The two equations of life — drag the divider between them:

before.label: photosynthesis
before.text: The uphill build: energy goes IN from light. CO₂ + water become sugar + oxygen — in chloroplasts.

after.label: respiration
after.text: The downhill burn: energy comes OUT as ATP. Glucose + oxygen become CO₂ + water — in mitochondria.

config.why: Near-mirror images, completely different machinery — no single factory could run both in one room, so ATP shuttles between them like money between accounts.

activities.anchor: The veins, finally, are the logistics
activities.caption: pair each leaf layer with its job
activities.name: phLeafMatch

config.prompt: A factory arranged in layers — pair each part with its job:

pairs.right: upright packed cells crammed with chloroplasts, where the light is brightest
loose, with air spaces so CO₂ diffuses to every photosynthesising cell
swell with water to open the stoma, sag to close it
carries water up from the roots — raw material and turgor
ships the finished sucrose to shoots, fruit and storage

config.why: Every layer answers the same three demands — light in, CO₂ in, water managed. A typical leaf carries 100+ stomata per square millimetre: a deliberate trade of water for carbon.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the two stages
activities.name: phStagesCloze

config.text: In the %%0%% stage, chlorophyll absorbs photons and the energy rips %%1%% molecules apart — the oxygen you breathe is this step's waste product. The captured energy is banked as ATP and NADPH. In the %%2%% stage (the %%3%% cycle), that banked energy fixes CO₂ until glucose emerges — it needs the first stage's products, but not the light itself.
config.hint: One stage needs photons; the other needs the bank.

activities.anchor: respires roughly 20% of your resting energy
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the brain's energy bill
activities.name: phBrainEstimate

config.prompt: Your brain is about 2% of your body weight. Roughly what share of your resting energy does it respire?
config.why: Roughly 20% — and your body recycles roughly its own weight of ATP molecules every day, recharging and spending them in continuous cycles.
config.context: Photosynthesis is income, respiration is salary day, ATP is the currency every purchase is made in.

activities.anchor: Other organisms run the anaerobic route differently
activities.caption: file the fermenters by their product
activities.name: phFermentBuckets

config.prompt: One emergency chemistry, different products — file each by what it makes:

items.label: bacteria turning milk into yogurt and cheese
yeast in beer, wine and bread
the CO₂ that puffs the dough

config.why: Yeast reduces pyruvate to ethanol and CO₂; human muscle converts it to lactic acid — same emergency logic, different enzymes. No sprint brews beer in your legs.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the controls answer
activities.name: phControlSpot

config.prompt: This photosynthesis-experiment answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Destarch the plant in the dark for 48 hours first — then the iodine is an honest meter.
Cover part of a leaf with foil: only the uncovered half goes black — light is necessary.
Seal a leaf in a jar with soda-lime, which ADDS carbon dioxide to the air: it stays amber, proving CO₂ is necessary.
A variegated leaf goes black only where it was green — chlorophyll is necessary.
Glucose is converted to insoluble starch for storage, which is what the iodine detects.
config.correction: Soda-lime SCRUBS CO₂ from the air — the leaf stays amber because the gas was removed, not added.
config.why: Three controls, three conclusions: foil removes light, soda-lime removes CO₂, variegation removes chlorophyll — each necessity shown by taking the factor away.
